find: the Court unanimously overruled \textit{Kentucky v.\ Dennison} and held that federal courts may order a governor by mandamus to perform the mandatory duty to surrender a fugitive, and that Puerto Rico may enforce that duty under the federal Extradition Act
replace: the Court held unanimously that Puerto Rico could obtain a federal court order enforcing the Governor's mandatory duty under the Extradition Act, overruling \textit{Kentucky v.\ Dennison} to the extent it made that statutory duty unenforceable. Six Justices reached the same conclusion under the Extradition Clause
reason: Dennison's mandatory-duty holding survived. Three Justices did not join the constitutional holding.

find: and joined in part by Justice Scalia.
replace: and joined by Justice Scalia as to the application of the Extradition Act and the overruling of \textit{Dennison}'s interpretation of its predecessor.
reason: The official syllabus says Scalia joined in part. His separate opinion identifies the portions he joined by subject, without listing them by section.

find: \emph{Michigan v.\ Doran} limits the asylum State's review to whether the papers are in order and the person is the charged fugitive
replace: \emph{Michigan v.\ Doran} limits review after the asylum State's governor grants extradition to whether the papers are facially in order, a crime has been charged in the demanding State, the detainee is the person named, and the detainee is a fugitive
reason: Doran specified four inquiries on habeas review of a grant of extradition.

find: overruling \emph{Dennison} as an interpretation of the 1793 statute's predecessor
replace: overruling \emph{Dennison} insofar as it interpreted the 1793 Act, the predecessor of \S~3182
reason: Garbled (reviewer concern): Scalia joined the portions 'overruling Kentucky v. Dennison ... insofar as it interpreted the predecessor of that statute' (i.e., of 18 U.S.C. 3182). The 1793 Act is itself the predecessor; it has no predecessor at issue.
